verified_facts.text: Alila Shanghai is at 500 Weihai Road in Shanghai's historic Jing'an district.
verified_facts.excerpt: Alila Shanghai places you in the historic Jing’an district

verified_facts.text: The hotel is within walking distance or a short drive of Shanghai Grand Theatre, People's Park and Shanghai Museum, and close to Nanjing Road shopping.
verified_facts.excerpt: enjoy being within walking distance or a short drive to several Shanghai attractions, such as Shanghai Grand Theatre, People’s Park, Shanghai Museum and more. You’re also close to the bustling shopping street of Nanjing Road

verified_facts.text: The hotel overlooks the historic Zhangyuan Shikumen compound.
verified_facts.excerpt: a prime location overlooking the historic Zhangyuan Shikumen

verified_facts.text: Design elements throughout the rooms celebrate Chinese craftsmanship and culture while embodying Shanghai's blend of modernity and tradition.
verified_facts.excerpt: Design elements throughout Alila Shanghai’s 186 rooms, which include 94 suites, celebrate Chinese craftsmanship and culture while embodying Shanghai’s blend of modernity and tradition.

verified_facts.text: The fourth-floor lobby is a light-flooded sky courtyard with pathways, waterworks and gardens around a ceramic and stainless steel tree sculpture by local artist Oscar Wang.
verified_facts.excerpt: you arrive in a light-flooded courtyard in the sky, a mesh of swirling pathways, mirror-flat waterworks, and manicured gardens surrounding a 17-foot tree made from ceramic and stainless steel by local artist Oscar Wang

verified_facts.text: Interiors by Beijing-based designer Ju Bin riff on traditional Chinese courtyard homes and the East-meets-West style of old Shanghai's shikumen houses.
verified_facts.excerpt: a fresh look that riffs on traditional Chinese courtyard homes and the East-meets-West style of old Shanghai's shikumen houses

verified_facts.text: Alila Shanghai is Alila's first urban outpost in China.
verified_facts.excerpt: As Alila's first urban outpost in China, it perfectly captures the resort-style hotel concept the brand is known for.

verified_facts.text: Rooms have natural finishes and a spa-like bathroom with Shanghai-inspired detailing, from textured glass to bold floor tiles.
verified_facts.excerpt: Enjoy the natural finishes and spa-like bathroom with Shanghai-inspired detailing, from textured glass to bold floor tiles.

verified_facts.text: Shikumen View rooms overlook Zhangyuan's shikumen rooftops, and one room type adds a private terrace.
verified_facts.excerpt: Unwind in this spacious 39-square-meter room that offers a stunning view of Zhangyuan’s shikumen rooftops, complete with a private terrace

verified_facts.text: The Penthouse Suite is on the hotel's highest floor.
verified_facts.excerpt: For the ultimate indulgence, opt for the 244 sqm Penthouse Suite King on the hotel’s highest floor.

verified_facts.text: A Childhood Dream-themed Family Suite has a king bed and a bunk bed, plus a welcome gift and children's amenities.
verified_facts.excerpt: With a welcome gift and children's amenities, every night's dream becomes the next destination.

verified_facts.text: On Level 5, an indoor infinity pool overlooks the hotel's green garden, alongside a hydrotherapy pool and a wet sauna.
verified_facts.excerpt: On Level 5, a 20-meter infinity pool overlooks the hotel’s green garden. Elsewhere, visitors will discover loungers, a hydrotherapy pool and a wet sauna.

verified_facts.text: Spa Alila blends modern healing therapies with traditional Eastern practices, offering massages, facials, herbal scrubs and body wraps.
verified_facts.excerpt: tailor a range of innovative treatments, including blissful massages, rejuvenating facials, herbal scrubs and body wraps. Blending modern healing therapies and traditional Eastern practices

verified_facts.text: The 24-hour fitness center has green garden views.
verified_facts.excerpt: Our well-equipped 24-hour fitness center with green garden views

verified_facts.text: A Lobby Level library holds a curated collection of books on Shanghai's history and culture.
verified_facts.excerpt: Within this space on the Lobby Level, a curated collection of books showcase Shanghai’s history and culture

verified_facts.text: 500 Weihai Road is the hotel's Chinese restaurant, integrating seafood into traditional Shanghai cuisine with sustainable, seasonal ingredients.
verified_facts.excerpt: This Chinese restaurant seamlessly integrates seafood into traditional Shanghai cuisine, placing a strong emphasis on the use of sustainable and seasonal ingredients.

verified_facts.text: Secret Roof serves coffee by day and handcrafted coffee cocktails by night with views of historical Zhangyuan.
verified_facts.excerpt: Enjoy expertly brewed coffee by day and handcrafted coffee cocktails by night alongside views of historical Zhangyuan at Secret Roof at Alila Shanghai.

verified_facts.text: Chayan@5th serves afternoon tea with brews by a resident tea master.
verified_facts.excerpt: Indulge in exquisite afternoon tea at Chayan@5th at Alila Shanghai. Enjoy sweet and savory delicacies accompanied by expert brews by the resident tea master.

verified_facts.text: A complimentary gong sound bath is offered to in-house guests as an Alila Moment.
verified_facts.excerpt: Escape the noise of modern life and slip into sonic stillness during this complimentary gong sound bath.

verified_facts.text: An Alila Moment takes guests to Lei Yun Shang, a Chinese medicine clinic founded in 1734, for a personal consultation with a senior practitioner.
verified_facts.excerpt: Enter Lei Yun Shang, a renowned TCM clinic founded in 1734, and explore its storied role in healing.

verified_facts.text: Guests can make their own pankou knot button with a master tailor at LongFeng Cheongsam Studio.
verified_facts.excerpt: Guided by a master tailor, you’ll make your own knot button, then try on a custom-fit garment.

verified_facts.text: An incense experience lets guests create their own incense blend under the guidance of a master.
verified_facts.excerpt: Under the guidance of a master, you’ll create your own incense blend using time-honored ingredients

verified_facts.text: The hotel no longer provides bottled water or disposable in-room amenities; guests are advised to bring their own essentials and a drinking vessel.
verified_facts.excerpt: our hotel no longer provides bottled water or disposable in-room amenities for staying guests. We recommend bringing your own essentials and a drinking vessel to refill with drinking water available throughout the hotel.

verified_facts.text: The hotel recommends local mapping apps such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map, as international mapping apps may not be accurate in mainland China.
verified_facts.excerpt: we recommend using local mapping applications such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map. International mapping apps may not be accurate in Chinese Mainland.

verified_facts.text: Guests must wear a swimming cap in the pool.
verified_facts.excerpt: do note that you'll need to wear a swimming cap before jumping in

verified_facts.text: East-facing rooms on high floors can glimpse The Bund's skyline on the horizon; views vary by floor and direction.
verified_facts.excerpt: views vary depending on the floor and rooms' direction—aim for an East-facing room on a high floor if you want a glimpse of The Bund's
